tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__add_repo
tools.description:
Add a GitHub repository to the current session so you can read, clone, or operate on it alongside the repos already in the session. Call this whenever you need a repository the session does not have — including when someone only asks a question about one, rather than asking for it to be attached. Prefer attaching a repository over reporting that you cannot reach it. 

IMPORTANT — DO NOT PRE-CHECK THE REPO BEFORE CALLING THIS TOOL. Do not curl github.com, do not run `gh repo view`, do not run `git ls-remote` to verify the repo exists. Unauthenticated requests to private repos return 404 ("Not Found") even when the repo is real and your session has authorized access to it. Those preemptive 404s will mislead you into skipping the tool. Instead: call add_repo with the owner/repo exactly as you have it. The backend performs the real reachability + authorization check and returns a structured error you can act on. If the repo genuinely doesn't exist or isn't accessible, the tool response will tell you — report that to the user. If it does exist, the tool response will include a clone command you can then run. Do not report success until the tool has actually been called and returned. 

WHEN ACCESS IS DENIED: if the tool returns an authorization or policy error — the repo exists but isn't enabled for this workspace/project/organization, or the GitHub App isn't installed or linked — relay the tool's exact reason to the user. The response names the remedy: if Claude doesn't have GitHub access for this organization at all, the user should reconnect GitHub under claude.ai Settings → Connectors; if the repo is simply not in the allowed set, a Claude.ai organization owner can grant access in the settings page the response points to. Do not add settings URLs beyond those provided here or in the tool response. Do not retry the same repo. You may remind the user which repositories are already available in this session, and offer to help them request access. Do not guess, infer, or list repositories you cannot see in the tool res… [truncated]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__create_trigger
tools.description: Create a Routine (scheduled trigger). Three targeting modes: (1) default — fires into THIS SESSION, resuming the same conversation each time; (2) persistent_session_id set — fires into a SPECIFIC OTHER SESSION you name (must be in your account); (3) create_new_session_on_fire=true — spawns a FRESH SESSION in this environment on each firing. Use mode 1 for recurring work you want to pick back up yourself; mode 2 for waking a sibling session you created; mode 3 when each firing should start from a clean slate. If the result warns that the Routine stores no connectors, say so plainly when you confirm the Routine to the user and pass on the remedy it names; never report such a Routine as simply created.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__list_triggers
tools.description: List Routines (scheduled triggers) owned by this account. Use it to find trigger IDs (trig_...) for update_trigger and delete_trigger. Each entry has the Routine's id, name, cron_expression, run_once_at, enabled state, ended_reason, next_run_at, created_at, persistent_session_id, and last_run. last_run is the most recent recorded run {status, fired_at, finished_at, session_id}. It is absent when no run was recorded (e.g. never fired). For a Routine that wakes an existing session, last_run records that the wake was delivered (SUCCEEDED) or failed to deliver, not how the turn went, unless run tracking covers that session. A FAILED or repeatedly non-SUCCEEDED last_run means the Routine is not doing its job. ended_reason says why a disabled Routine is permanently disabled. suspension_reason (e.g. subscription_paused) marks a temporary hold that lifts when the owner's subscription resumes. Both empty means user-paused. One-shot Routines that already fired (e.g. delivered send_later reminders) are hidden unless include_completed is true. Scheduled tasks stored locally by the Cowork desktop app are not listed.

(* AplCore -- see AplCore.fsi.  The redesign of v1/base/AplCore.fss, promoted to
   the base on 2026-09-13: APL's values are Fortress's OWN arrays, not a wrapper.

   An APL scalar is an RR64; a vector is an Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] from
   array[\RR64\](n); a matrix is an Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] from
   array[\RR64\](r,c) (merged ledger row 57).  Rank is not a field, it is the
   TYPE, and every primitive is an overload family keyed on rank:

       f(x: RR64)                         rank 0
       f[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\])    rank 1
       f[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\])   rank 2

   This works -- and only this spelling works.  Overloading directly on
   Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] against Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] is rejected ("first
   parameters m:[...] and v:[...] are unrelated (neither subtype, excludes, nor
   equal)", r01_native.out), because two instantiations of one generic trait are
   not known to exclude.  Vector and Matrix reach Rank1 and Rank2, which DO
   exclude each other (FortressLibrary.fsi:1072-1076), and the nat is inferred
   from the runtime-built array (r02a_rankover.out).  Parameters are therefore
   Vector/Matrix; RESULTS are Array[\...\], the honest runtime-sized type.

   What the library does for us, for no lines at all: + and - elementwise on
   equal-length vectors and on matrices (Vector.+, Matrix.+), pmul, DOT, m.t(),
   |v|, v[i], m[i,j], u <- v, comprehensions, SUM, PROD, BIG MAX, and a LENGTH
   ERROR by dispatch when the two nats disagree (r09_reduce.out).

   Index origin is 0, as the chapter sets it with its first line, ⎕IO ← 0. *)
component AplCore
export AplCore

(* ------------------------------------------------------------- numbers ---- *)
(* RR64 -> ZZ32 in one line: there is still no narrowing (apl/gaps.md row 10),
   but the floor bracket's ZZ64 stringifies as an integer (row 11) and
   strToInt reads it back.  v1/base/AplCore.fss spent 14 lines on this. *)
aplInt(v: RR64): ZZ32 = strToInt("" (|\ v /|))

aplNegS(v: RR64): RR64 = -v

(* APL's high minus for negatives; integral values print without a fraction *)
aplFmt(v: RR64): String =
    if v < 0.0 then ("¯" aplFmt(-v))
    elif (1.0 (|\ v /|)) = v then ("" (|\ v /|))
    else ("" v) end

aplPad(s: String, w: ZZ32): String = do
    r: String := s
    while |r| < w do r := (" " r) end
    r
  end

(* ------------------------------------------------------- constructors ----- *)
aplVec(n: ZZ32, f: ZZ32 -> RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = array[\RR64\](n).fill(f)
aplMat(r: ZZ32, c: ZZ32, f: (ZZ32,ZZ32) -> RR64): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    array[\RR64\](r,c).fill(f)
aplZilde(): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = array[\RR64\](0)

(* strand notation, built right to left by the grammar: the tail of a strand is
   a scalar when it has one element and a vector when it has more, so one
   overload each and no length bookkeeping in the grammar. *)
aplCons(x: RR64, y: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    aplVec(2, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => if i = 0 then x else y end)
aplCons[\nat s\](x: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    aplVec(|v| + 1, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => if i = 0 then x else v[i - 1] end)

(* ----------------------------------------------------------- display ----- *)
aplShow(x: RR64): String = aplFmt(x)

aplShow[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): String =
    if |v| = 0 then "" else (BIG |||[ i <- seq(0 # |v|) ] aplFmt(v[i])) end

(* Dyalog's matrix display: one line per row, each column padded to its own
   width (apl/gaps.md row 14, now over the library's own matrix). *)
aplShow[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): String = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    if (rows = 0) OR (cols = 0) then ""
    else
        w = array[\ZZ32\](cols).fill(
                fn (k: ZZ32): ZZ32 => BIG MAX[ i <- seq(0 # rows) ] |aplFmt(m[i,k])|)
        BIG //[ i <- seq(0 # rows) ]
            (BIG |||[ k <- seq(0 # cols) ] aplPad(aplFmt(m[i,k]), w[k]))
    end
  end

(* ------------------------------------------------------------- ⍳ iota ---- *)
aplIota(n: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] requires { n >= 0.0 } =
    aplVec(aplInt(n), fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => 1.0 i)

(* --------------------------------------------------- ⍴ monadic: shape ---- *)
aplShapeOf(x: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = aplZilde()
aplShapeOf[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    aplVec(1, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => 1.0 |v|)
aplShapeOf[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    aplVec(2, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => if i = 0 then 1.0 rows else 1.0 cols end)
  end

(* --------------------------------------------------- ⍴ dyadic: reshape --- *)
(* The RESULT's rank is the LENGTH of the left argument, a runtime value -- the
   one place where APL's rank is not in the type.  The grammar reads it off the
   source text instead: `2 4⍴x` fires aplReshapeM, `4⍴x` fires aplReshapeV, so
   the rank is fixed at expansion time and never at run time. *)
aplReshapeV(n: RR64, x: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] requires { n >= 0.0 } =
    aplVec(aplInt(n), fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => x)
aplReshapeV[\nat s\](n: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]
        requires { (n >= 0.0) AND (|v| > 0) } =
    aplVec(aplInt(n), fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => v[i MOD |v|])

aplReshapeM(rw: RR64, cl: RR64, x: RR64): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]
        requires { (rw >= 0.0) AND (cl >= 0.0) } =
    aplMat(aplInt(rw), aplInt(cl), fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => x)
aplReshapeM[\nat s\](rw: RR64, cl: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]
        requires { (rw >= 0.0) AND (cl >= 0.0) AND (|v| > 0) } = do
    c = aplInt(cl)
    aplMat(aplInt(rw), c, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => v[((c i) + j) MOD |v|])
  end
aplReshapeM[\nat r, nat c\](rw: RR64, cl: RR64, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]):
        Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] requires { (rw >= 0.0) AND (cl >= 0.0) } = do
    (mr, mc) = m.sizes
    cc = aplInt(cl)
    aplMat(aplInt(rw), cc, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => do
        k = ((cc i) + j) MOD (mr mc)
        m[k DIV mc, k MOD mc]
      end)
  end

(* ------------------------------------------- scalar extension: × ÷ + - --- *)

   `requires` clause cannot destructure m.sizes *)
aplRowsOf[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): ZZ32 = do (rows, cols) = m.sizes; rows end
aplColsOf[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): ZZ32 = do (rows, cols) = m.sizes; cols end

(* --------------------------------------------- the elementwise skeletons --- *)
(* Every comparison, every Boolean connective and every matrix arithmetic op is
   one of these six zips with a scalar function, so each opr below is one line. *)
aplZipV[\nat s, nat t\](f: (RR64,RR64)->RR64, a: Vector[\RR64,s\], b: Vector[\RR64,t\]):
        Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] requires { |a| = |b| } =
    aplVec(|a|, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => f(a[i], b[i]))
aplZipSV[\nat s\](f: (RR64,RR64)->RR64, a: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    v.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => f(a, x))
aplZipVS[\nat s\](f: (RR64,RR64)->RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\], a: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    v.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => f(x, a))
aplZipM[\nat r, nat c, nat p, nat q\](f: (RR64,RR64)->RR64, a: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\],
        b: Matrix[\RR64,p,q\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]
        requires { (aplRowsOf(a) = aplRowsOf(b)) AND (aplColsOf(a) = aplColsOf(b)) } = do
    (ar, ac) = a.sizes
    aplMat(ar, ac, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => f(a[i,j], b[i,j]))
  end
aplZipSM[\nat r, nat c\](f: (RR64,RR64)->RR64, a: RR64, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]):
        Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = m.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => f(a, x))
aplZipMS[\nat r, nat c\](f: (RR64,RR64)->RR64, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], a: RR64):
        Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = m.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => f(x, a))

aplEqS(x: RR64, y: RR64): RR64 = if x = y then 1.0 else 0.0 end
aplNeS(x: RR64, y: RR64): RR64 = if x =/= y then 1.0 else 0.0 end
aplLtS(x: RR64, y: RR64): RR64 = if x < y then 1.0 else 0.0 end
aplLeS(x: RR64, y: RR64): RR64 = if x <= y then 1.0 else 0.0 end
aplGtS(x: RR64, y: RR64): RR64 = if x > y then 1.0 else 0.0 end
aplGeS(x: RR64, y: RR64): RR64 = if x >= y then 1.0 else 0.0 end
aplAndS(x: RR64, y: RR64): RR64 = if (x =/= 0.0) AND (y =/= 0.0) then 1.0 else 0.0 end
aplOrS(x: RR64, y: RR64): RR64 = if (x =/= 0.0) OR (y =/= 0.0) then 1.0 else 0.0 end
aplMaxS(x: RR64, y: RR64): RR64 = if x > y then x else y end
aplMinS(x: RR64, y: RR64): RR64 = if x < y then x else y end

aplPowS(x: RR64, y: RR64): RR64 = x^y

   directly on the library's own Vector/Matrix families, with scalar
   extension.  Values stay the library's arrays; nothing is wrapped. *)
component alg_a
export Executable
import System.{...}

(* ==================== ALGEBRA DECLARATIONS (counted) ==================== *)
vecOf(n: ZZ32, f: ZZ32 -> RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = array[\RR64\](n).fill(f)
matOf(r: ZZ32, c: ZZ32, f: (ZZ32,ZZ32) -> RR64): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    array[\RR64\](r,c).fill(f)
zipV[\nat s, nat t\](f: (RR64,RR64)->RR64, a: Vector[\RR64,s\], b: Vector[\RR64,t\]):
        Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = vecOf(|a|, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => f(a[i], b[i]))
zipM[\nat r, nat c, nat p, nat q\](f: (RR64,RR64)->RR64, a: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\],
        b: Matrix[\RR64,p,q\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (rows, cols) = a.sizes
    matOf(rows, cols, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => f(a[i,j], b[i,j]))
  end
mulS(x: RR64, y: RR64): RR64 = x y
divS(x: RR64, y: RR64): RR64 = x / y
maxS(x: RR64, y: RR64): RR64 = if x > y then x else y end
gtS(x: RR64, y: RR64): RR64 = if x > y then 1.0 else 0.0 end
eqS(x: RR64, y: RR64): RR64 = if x = y then 1.0 else 0.0 end

(* Hadamard *)
opr ×[\nat s, nat t\](a: Vector[\RR64,s\], b: Vector[\RR64,t\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = zipV(mulS, a, b)
opr ×[\nat r, nat c, nat p, nat q\](a: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], b: Matrix[\RR64,p,q\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = zipM(mulS, a, b)

(* elementwise / with scalar extension in both orders *)
opr /[\nat s, nat t\](a: Vector[\RR64,s\], b: Vector[\RR64,t\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = zipV(divS, a, b)
opr /[\nat r, nat c, nat p, nat q\](a: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], b: Matrix[\RR64,p,q\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = zipM(divS, a, b)
opr /[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\], a: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = v.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => x / a)
opr /[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], a: RR64): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = m.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => x / a)
opr /[\nat s\](a: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = v.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => a / x)
opr /[\nat r, nat c\](a: RR64, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = m.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => a / x)

(* + and - between an array and a scalar, both orders (array+array is the library's) *)
opr +[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\], a: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = v.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => x + a)
opr +[\nat s\](a: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = v.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => a + x)
opr +[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], a: RR64): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = m.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => x + a)
opr +[\nat r, nat c\](a: RR64, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = m.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => a + x)
opr -[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\], a: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = v.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => x - a)
opr -[\nat s\](a: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = v.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => a - x)
opr -[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], a: RR64): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = m.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => x - a)
opr -[\nat r, nat c\](a: RR64, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = m.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => a - x)

(* elementwise SQRT, exp, log *)
opr SQRT[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = v.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => SQRT x)
opr SQRT[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = m.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => SQRT x)
exp[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = v.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => exp x)
exp[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = m.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => exp x)
log[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = v.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => log x)
log[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = m.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => log x)

(* MAX with a scalar, both orders, and between two matrices *)
opr MAX[\nat r, nat c\](a: RR64, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = m.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => maxS(a, x))
opr MAX[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], a: RR64): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = m.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => maxS(x, a))
opr MAX[\nat r, nat c, nat p, nat q\](a: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], b: Matrix[\RR64,p,q\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = zipM(maxS, a, b)

(* comparisons against a scalar yield a 0/1 matrix *)
opr >[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], a: RR64): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = m.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => gtS(x, a))
opr =[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], a: RR64): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = m.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => eqS(x, a))

(* the transpose postfix of gap row 149 *)
opr (m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\])^T[\nat r, nat c\]: Matrix[\RR64,c,r\] = m.t()
(* ==================== END ALGEBRA DECLARATIONS ========================== *)

showV[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): String = BIG |||[i <- seq(0#|v|)] ("" v[i])
showM[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): String = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    BIG //[i <- seq(0#rows)] (BIG |||[j <- seq(0#cols)] ("" m[i,j]))
  end

beta1: RR64 = 0.85
beta2: RR64 = 0.99
epsAdam: RR64 = 10.0^(-8)
eps: RR64 = 10.0^(-5)

(* ---------------------------- the five formulas ------------------------- *)
adam(p: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], m: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], v: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\],
     g: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], t: ZZ32, lr: RR64):
     (Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]) = do
    m' = beta1 m + (1 - beta1) g
    v' = beta2 v + (1 - beta2) (g × g)
    p' = p - (lr (m' / (1 - beta1^t))) / ((SQRT (v' / (1 - beta2^t))) + epsAdam)
    (p', m', v')
  end

softmax[\nat s\](z: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
    e = exp(z - (BIG MAX[t <- z] t))
    e / (SUM[t <- e] t)
  end

rmsnorm[\nat s\](x: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    x / SQRT (eps + (x DOT x) / |x|)

run(): () = do
    n = 6
    p = vecOf(n, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => 0.1 (1.0 i))
    mm = vecOf(n, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => 0.01 (1.0 i))
    vv = vecOf(n, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => 0.001 (1.0 (i + 1)))
    gg = vecOf(n, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => 0.5 - 0.1 (1.0 i))
    println "== 1 Adam (vectors of 6, t = 3, lr = 0.01) =="
    (p', m', v') = adam(p, mm, vv, gg, 3, 0.01)
    println "m' = " showV(m')
    println "v' = " showV(v')
    println "p' = " showV(p')

    z = vecOf(n, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => 1.0 i - 2.0)
    println "== 2 softmax =="
    println "z  = " showV(z)
    println "sm = " showV(softmax(z))

    println "== 3 rmsnorm =="
    println "x  = " showV(z)
    println "rn = " showV(rmsnorm(z))

    m0 = matOf(4, 3, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => 1.0 (2 i + j) - 3.0)
    f2 = matOf(3, 3, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => 0.1 (1.0 (i + 2 j)))
    dX4 = matOf(4, 3, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => 0.5 - 0.1 (1.0 (i j)))
    println "== 4 ReLU and its backward (4x3, 3x3) =="
    mr = 0.0 MAX m0
    println "m0 =" //showM(m0)
    println "mr =" //showM(mr)
    dM0 = (dX4 f2) × (m0 > 0.0)
    println "dM0 =" //showM(dM0)

    xp = matOf(4, 3, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => 1.0 (i + j))
    hc = matOf(4, 3, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => 0.25 (1.0 (i + 1)))
    wo = matOf(3, 3, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => if i = j then 1.0 else 0.5 end)
    println "== 5 residual: x2 = xp + hc (wo^T) =="
    x2 = xp + hc (wo^T)
    println "x2 =" //showM(x2)
    println "2.0 v = " showV(2.0 z)
    println "v 2.0 = " showV(z 2.0)
    println "2.0 m =" //showM(2.0 m0)

    (* timing: Adam over a 4192-vector, 100 repetitions *)
    big = 4192
    pb: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] := vecOf(big, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => 0.001 (1.0 i))
    mb: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] := vecOf(big, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => 0.0)
    vb: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] := vecOf(big, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => 0.0)
    gb = vecOf(big, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => 0.5 - 0.0001 (1.0 i))
    t0 = nanoTime()
    for k <- seq(0#100) do
        (pb, mb, vb) := adam(pb, mb, vb, gb, 1, 0.01)
    end
    println "adam 4192 x 100: " ((nanoTime() - t0) DIV 1000000) " ms  (pb[0] = " pb[0] ")"
  end
end
